plain_language_summary: Terahertz refers to a part of the electromagnetic spectrum between microwave and infrared ranges.
educational_notes: Consumer wellness references should avoid overstating what terahertz devices can do and should explain the category conservatively.
safety_framing: Educational reference only. Spectrum education is not a treatment claim.

plain_language_summary: Terahertz and infrared are different parts of the electromagnetic spectrum and should not be treated as identical.
educational_notes: Infrared is commonly associated with heat-based wellness routines, while terahertz is a separate emerging category.
safety_framing: Avoid assuming different spectrum categories have the same use, effect, or safety profile.

plain_language_summary: Terahertz, red light, and infrared are separate spectrum categories with different consumer device contexts.
educational_notes: Red light is often discussed for skin-facing routines. Infrared is often discussed for heat or deeper exposure contexts. Terahertz is a separate emerging category.
safety_framing: Educational reference only. Device-specific instructions should guide use.

plain_language_summary: Handheld terahertz devices are designed for targeted at-home wellness sessions.
educational_notes: Device design, distance, session length, and user comfort should guide beginner use.
safety_framing: Start conservatively and follow device instructions. Stop use if discomfort occurs.

plain_language_summary: Beginners should use terahertz wellness devices conservatively and avoid aggressive or prolonged use.
educational_notes: Short, conservative sessions are a safer starting point than long or intense routines.
safety_framing: Pregnancy, implanted medical devices, serious health conditions, or uncertainty should prompt consultation with a qualified professional.

plain_language_summary: Terahertz wellness devices should not be used as replacements for medical care.
